Ever mixed bentonite into water and got nothing back?
Bentonite clay is made of thousands of flat plates stacked together. In clean fresh water, sodium sitting on those plates pulls water in between the layers and forces them apart, that's what opens the clay up.

That swelling is what gives your fluid its body: gel strength, everything it needs to do down the hole.

Hard or salty water carries calcium and other minerals that grab the same spots on the plate before the sodium gets there. Calcium doesn't pull water in the same way, so the plates stay tight and the clay barely swells.

Same bag, same water volume, nowhere near the performance. The clay never got the chance to open up.
Ever mixed a batch that just wouldn't build body, no matter how much you added?

Get the water right first. Everything after that is easy.
HDD Gel is the sodium bentonite that handles suspension and wall-sealing on standard HDD, tunnelling and waterwell work. It's the quickest to mix in the range, built for everyday ground, not the toughest bores.

Condition the water before it goes in. Hard or salty water stops the clay swelling properly, so sort that first. One bag per 1,000L is the normal mix from there.

You know what you're getting every bag: easy to mix, predictable performance.

Long, difficult bores needing the highest gel strength still call for Max Gel or Max Bore. Everywhere else in standard work, HDD Gel does the job.
Not sure if your water needs conditioning before you mix? Give the team a call.
